items.title: opensandbox-group / OpenSandbox
items.summary: OpenSandbox is an Agentic AI Foundation project that provides isolated environments for AI agents to execute code, run commands, and manage files on local Docker or Kubernetes infrastructure. It supports multiple programming languages via SDKs and offers features like network access control and a credential vault.
items.why_it_matters: It enables the execution of AI agent workloads in isolated environments with specific controls for network egress and credential management.
items.next_step_detail: pip install opensandbox && run `opensandbox --help` to evaluate integration.

items.title: Muse Ember: Our smallest, most efficient model
items.summary: Meta released Muse Ember, its smallest and most efficient model, designed for complex reasoning, tool calls, and long-document parsing. It offers a 1M-token context window and costs $0.10 per million input tokens and $0.50 per million output tokens.
items.why_it_matters: Muse Ember matches Claude Haiku 5.5's best score at about a third of the cost and beats every GPT-6 Luna setting, positioning it on the efficiency frontier of the Artificial Analysis leaderboard.
items.next_step_detail: Benchmark Muse Ember against your current model on tool‑call latency and cost per token.

items.title: Take a Claude Agent SDK agent from install to deploy with Agents CLI
items.summary: The guide shows how to use the Claude Agent SDK together with Google Cloud Agents CLI to deploy an agent to Cloud Run with tracing and evaluation built‑in.
items.why_it_matters: Provides a production‑ready, end‑to‑end pipeline for shipping autonomous agents to the cloud.
items.next_step_detail: Follow the article steps; run `gcloud agents deploy <your‑agent>` after installing the CLI.

items.title: My coding agent almost wiped my git repo. Here's what I built to stop it.
items.summary: Describes a dual‑mode CLI that adds a blast‑radius firewall and watchdog to prevent autonomous coding agents from damaging a repository.
items.why_it_matters: Provides concrete safeguards you can adopt immediately for any autonomous coding agent you run.
items.next_step_detail: Clone the repo and run the provided CLI wrapper on your own coding agents.

items.title: Introducing NovaDesk AI: Building a Stateful Hotel Concierge with LangGraph
items.summary: The article walks through building a stateful hotel‑concierge agent using LangGraph, demonstrating persistent memory and tool use.
items.why_it_matters: Shows a production‑grade pattern for multi‑step, stateful agents that can be adapted to any domain.
items.next_step_detail: Follow the tutorial and run the provided LangGraph example locally.

items.title: stablyai/orca
items.summary: Orca enables running a fleet of coding agents (e.g., Claude Code, Codex) using your own subscription, with support for desktop, mobile, and remote runtimes.
items.why_it_matters: Provides a ready‑to‑use multi‑agent framework for building autonomous coding assistants in Python projects.
items.next_step_detail: Clone the repo and run the quick‑start script to spin up a sample coding agent.

items.title: anthropics / claude-plugins-official
items.summary: Official repository of high‑quality Claude Code plugins maintained by Anthropic.
items.why_it_matters: Provides vetted plugins that can be integrated into Python‑based autonomous agents for extended capabilities.
items.next_step_detail: Compare this plugin directory against your current toolset and consider adding `pip install anthropic-plugins`.

items.title: TPU 8tx and TPU 8i Max
items.summary: Google announces two new eighth‑generation TPU models: the 8tx for confidential inference and the 8i Max for massive context windows, targeting complex agentic workloads.
items.why_it_matters: Provides hardware options that can accelerate and secure large‑scale LLM agent pipelines you may deploy.
items.next_step_detail: Review the spec sheet and compare pricing with your current cloud GPU/TPU usage.

items.title: We Moved to a Bigger Model to Debug the Test. Then We Went Back to the Smaller One.
items.summary: The article announces agentpolicy v0.1.0, a local‑first, Cedar‑based policy decision point designed for AI agents, with a short walkthrough.
items.why_it_matters: A lightweight policy engine helps enforce safety and governance in autonomous agent pipelines.
items.next_step_detail: Install with `pip install agentpolicy` and run the quick‑start example.

items.title: snap-stanford / memorilla
items.summary: Memorilla provides a latent semantic memory layer for LLMs, enabling persistent context across calls without fine‑tuning.
items.why_it_matters: Persistent memory is a core capability for building autonomous agents that need long‑term state.
items.next_step_detail: Clone the repo and run `pip install -e .` to experiment with the memory API.

items.title: computer-use-rs: Open-Source Computer Use for Rust
items.summary: computer-use-rs is a Rust crate that enables code to see and control desktop applications, facilitating computer‑use capabilities for agents.
items.why_it_matters: Offers a performant alternative for building agent‑driven UI automation, useful for cross‑language stacks.
items.next_step_detail: Add `computer-use-rs = "*"` to Cargo.toml and run the example binary.

items.title: Locating the source of a mysterious beep
items.summary: The author used Claude Code to build a multi‑device system that triangulates a beep source, demonstrating a practical autonomous agent workflow.
items.why_it_matters: Shows a concrete example of stitching LLM‑driven agents with edge devices, directly applicable to building production‑grade agent pipelines.
items.next_step_detail: Clone the repo (if available) and run the provided script to see the agent orchestration in action.

items.title: Authorization Drift in LLM Agents: Evaluating Boundary Compliance in Multi-Step Tool Use
items.summary: Introduces the concept of authorization drift where LLM agents exceed their permission boundaries and provides a benchmark of 648 samples across seven domains.

items.next_step_detail: Download the Authorization Drift Benchmark and review the evaluation script.

items.title: HF Paper: LowRAM: Low-Rank Keys and Amortised Values for Composable KV Cache Compression at Test-Time
items.summary: Introduces LowRAM, a method to compress KV caches during inference using low‑rank factorization and amortised values.

items.title: Top 7 Best Agent Gateways

items.next_step_detail: Skim the list and bookmark any gateways that match your stack.

items.title: Claude Fable 5.2 and Mythos 5.2

items.title: soxoj / maigret

items.title: HF Paper: CPU-ARC: Agentic Reasoning Caching for on-CPU Reasoning Reuse

items.next_step_detail: Review the paper to assess if its caching approach fits your agent stack.

items.title: HF Paper: Steerable Multi-Objective Group-Relative Preference Optimization with Jointly Trained Low-Rank Adapters

items.title: How Much Training-Inference Mismatch Can On-Policy Distillation Tolerate?
